plan.title: AD skin treated vs control: DE genes + hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human skin bulk RNA-seq samples (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) as raw gene-level Salmon counts (12000 genes x 12 samples in counts.csv, condition in metadata.csv), with one flagged concern: sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median. The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 procedure for this situation: sample-structure QC first (sample_01 is kept through QC and removed only with a stated reason — depth alone is not a reason, since size factors account for it), then a minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage and BH/independent-filtering at alpha 0.05. Because replicate number is at the low-mid end, an edgeR quasi-likelihood run supplies the robustness overlap the report rules require (intersection = high-confidence set). Pathways are read out as over-representation analysis of the up- and down-regulated DE sets against the staged MSigDB Hallmark human 2026.1 collection with the tested genes as the explicit universe — the method check for this situation permits ORA (not preranked GSEA). No covariates, no batch term (single batch), no transcript-level analysis (only gene-level counts exist, so differential transcript usage is out of scope).

Minimal pre-filter: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples
